questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 30 days and 40 days, respectively. They began the work together but after a certain time, A leaves off and B completed the remaining work in 25 days. After how many days did A leave?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's work time = 30 days.

B's work time = 40 days.

B alone completes the remaining work in 25 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/30

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/40

Total work = 1 (Considering the whole work as a single unit)

**Calculation:**

Work done by B in the last 25 days = 25 × (1/40) = 25/40

Remaining work before B worked alone = 1 - 25/40 = 15/40 = 3/8

Let the number of days A and B worked together be x days.

Work done by A and B in x days = x × (1/30 + 1/40) = x × (70/1200) = x × (7/120)

⇒ x × (7/120) = 3/8

⇒ x = (3/8) × (120/7)

⇒ x = 360/56

⇒ x = 45/7

⇒ x = 6 (3/7) days

**A leaves after 6 (3/7) days.**

questions.question: 6 skilled workers can complete a work in 4 days. After three days 3 more skilled workers joined them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

6 skilled workers can complete a work in 4 days.

After three days, 3 more skilled workers joined them.

**Formula Used:**

Work done = Number of workers × Number of days

Remaining work = Total work - Work done

**Calculation:**

Total work = 6 workers × 4 days = 24 worker-days

Work done in 3 days = 6 workers × 3 days = 18 worker-days

Remaining work = 24 worker-days - 18 worker-days

⇒ Remaining work = 6 worker-days

After three days, total workers = 6 + 3 = 9 workers

Let the number of days to complete the remaining work be 'd' days.

9 workers × d days = 6 worker-days

⇒ d = 6 worker-days / 9 workers

⇒ d = (2)/(3) days

**They will now take (2)/(3) days to complete the remaining work.**

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 250 m. When the policeman starts chase, the thief also starts running. Assuming that the speed of the thief is 10 km/h and that of the policeman is 12.5 km/h. How far will have the thief run before he is caught?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 250 m.

Speed of the thief = 10 km/h.

Speed of the policeman = 12.5 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of the policeman - Speed of the thief.

Time = Distance / Speed.

**Calculation:**

First, convert speeds into m/s:

Speed of the thief = 10 × (1000/3600) = 10000/3600 m/s.

Speed of the policeman = 12.5 × (1000/3600) = 12500/3600 m/s.

Relative speed = (12500/3600) - (10000/3600) m/s.

Relative speed = 2500/3600 m/s.

Distance to be covered to catch the thief = 250 m.

Time = 250 / (2500/3600).

Time = 250 times (3600)/(2500).

Time = 360 {seconds}.

Distance run by the thief in this time = Time × Speed of the thief.

Distance = 360 × (10000/3600).

Distance = 1000 m.

**The thief will have run 1 km before he is caught.**

Average speed = Total distance travelled/Total Time

Initial ratio of three numbers = 1:2:3.

**Formula Used:**

Let the three numbers be x, 2x, and 3x respectively.

After adding 5 to each, the numbers become (x + 5), (2x + 5), and (3x + 5).

The new ratio is given by (x + 5):(2x + 5):(3x + 5) = 2:3:4.

After adding 5 to each, they become (x + 5), (2x + 5), and (3x + 5).

The new ratio is 2:3:4. Therefore,

⇒ (x + 5)/(2x + 5) = 2/3

And,

Using the first part of the new ratio to find x,

⇒ 3(x + 5) = 2(2x + 5)

⇒ 3x + 15 = 4x + 10

⇒ x = 5

**The smallest number is 5.**

questions.question: The distance between two towns is covered in 9 hours at a speed of 60 kmph. By how much should the speed (in km/h) be increased so that 1 hour of the travelling time is saved?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between two towns = Distance covered at 60 kmph in 9 hours.

Speed = 60 kmph, Time = 9 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

New speed = Original speed + Increase in speed

New time = Original time - Time saved

**Calculation:**

Distance = 60 kmph × 9 hours = 540 km

To save 1 hour, new time = 9 hours - 1 hour = 8 hours

Using Distance = New speed × New time

⇒ 540 = New speed × 8

⇒ New speed = 540 / 8 = 67.5 kmph

⇒ Increase in speed = New speed - Original speed

⇒ Increase in speed = 67.5 kmph - 60 kmph = 7.5 kmph

**The speed should be increased by 7.5 km/h.**

then, 5th May 2022 will be Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.

= 31 days → 31/7 = 4 weeks and 3 odd days.

So, **5th June 2022** will be Thursday + 3 = Sunday.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

• Money serves as a **store of value**, enabling individuals to save and defer consumption until a later date.

• Money functions as a **medium of exchange**, facilitating transactions between buyers and sellers.
 
• The **barter system** involves the direct exchange of goods and services without the use of money, which is different from the functions of money.

• The **barter system** was prevalent before the invention of money.
 
• While the barter system can work in small economies, it is inefficient in larger economies due to the **double coincidence of wants** problem, where two parties each possess an item the other wants.
 
• Money helps to overcome the limitations of the barter system by providing a common medium of exchange.
 
• By serving as a store of value, unit of account, and medium of exchange, money simplifies and enhances economic transactions.
 
• Modern economies rely on money to facilitate trade, savings, and economic calculation.
